Research interests

Learning through dynamics.

My research connects generative modeling, differential equations, and adaptive computation, with applications in computer vision and graph time series.

01

Efficient generative AI

I investigate how to control the computation used by diffusion models while retaining useful generative structure. My work explores input-adaptive generation, structured diffusion processes, and conditional image restoration.

Applications include image generation, rain removal, and forecasting wildfire risk over multiple future horizons.

  • Input-Adaptive Generative Dynamics in Diffusion Models
  • Spectral-Structured Diffusion for Single-Image Rain Removal
  • N-Tree Diffusion for Long-Horizon Wildfire Risk Forecasting
Current questions

How much computation does each input need?

How can the structure of a task inform the generation process?

02

Adaptive neural architectures

I study architectures that adjust computation to the input. Puppet-CNN represents convolutional parameters as a continuous dynamical system, generating layer parameters along a learned trajectory.

This perspective connects compact model storage with flexible, input-adaptive computation.

  • Puppet-CNN · ECCV 2026
03

Continuous-time neural modeling

I use neural differential equations to model motion and graph time series in continuous time. These models provide a natural way to work with irregular observations and evolving relationships.

My work includes hierarchical human pose forecasting, stochastic prediction on graphs, and unsupervised online denoising.

  • HDG-ODE · ICCV 2023
  • AGGDN · ICONIP 2023
  • ∞-Net · ICONIP 2024
